Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

questions.q: A ball of mass m strikes a rigid wall with speed u and rebounds with the same speed. The impulse imparted by the wall is —
questions.work: Taking the rebound direction as positive: Δp = mu − (−mu) = 2mu.

questions.q: A force of 5 N moves a body 20 m along its own direction. The work done is —
Sound of wavelength λ travelling at v m/s enters another medium where its speed is 2v m/s. The new wavelength is —
questions.work:
The frequency does not change, so λ ∝ v.
Speed doubles ⇒ λ' = 2λ.

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (fill in the blanks, true/false, match or one word).

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) Mass is a measure of ______. (b) Impulse equals the area under the ______–time graph.
Fill in the blanks: (a) Kirchhoff's junction rule is based on conservation of ______. (b) The loop rule is based on conservation of ______.
Fill in the blanks: (a) The angle of dip where the horizontal and vertical components of the earth's field are equal is ______. (b) ______ substances are feebly magnetised opposite to the field.
Fill in the blanks: (a) The induced current opposes the cause producing it — this is ______'s law. (b) Transformer cores are laminated to reduce ______ currents.
State True or False: (a) Angular dispersion for two colours is independent of the angle of the prism. (b) The angular width of the primary rainbow is more than that of the secondary.
questions.answer:
(a) False — angular dispersion (μ_v − μ_r)A grows with A.
(b) False — the primary bow is narrower.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: State Faraday's laws of electromagnetic induction.
questions.answer:
First law: whenever the magnetic flux linked with a circuit changes, an emf is induced in it.
Second law: the induced emf equals the rate of change of flux linkage: e = −N dφ/dt.

questions.q: Why do most ordinary gases not show dispersion of white light?
questions.answer: Their refractive index is very close to 1 and almost the same for all colours, so the colours are hardly separated.

questions.q: Find the polarizing angle for light incident from air on a medium of refractive index √3.
questions.answer: Brewster's law: tan iₚ = μ = √3 ⇒ iₚ = 60°.

questions.q: What were the drawbacks of Rutherford's model?
questions.answer: A revolving electron is accelerated, so by classical theory it should radiate energy continuously and spiral into the nucleus. Atoms would be unstable and would give a continuous spectrum — contrary to observed stable atoms and line spectra.

questions.q: Define (a) stopping potential and (b) threshold frequency.
questions.answer:
(a) Stopping potential: the minimum negative potential applied to the anode that stops the most energetic photoelectrons, so the photocurrent becomes zero (eV₀ = KE_max).
(b) Threshold frequency: the minimum frequency of incident light below which no photoelectrons are emitted from a given metal.

questions.q: A radioactive substance decays to 1/32 of its activity in 25 days. Calculate its half-life.
Out of fission and fusion, which converts mass into energy more efficiently, and why?
questions.answer: Fusion. Per unit mass of fuel it releases several times more energy (e.g. about 6.7 MeV per nucleon for hydrogen to helium, against about 0.85 MeV per nucleon for uranium fission), because light nuclei gain much more binding energy per nucleon when they fuse.

questions.q: How is the conductivity of a semiconductor affected by a rise in temperature? Explain.
questions.answer: It increases. More electrons gain enough energy to jump from the valence band to the conduction band, creating more free electrons and holes.

questions.q: Draw a circuit diagram of a stabilized power supply showing a step-down transformer, a full-wave rectifier, a capacitor filter and a Zener diode.
questions.answer: AC mains → step-down transformer → full-wave rectifier (bridge of four diodes) → a capacitor across the output (filter) → a series resistor and a Zener diode in reverse bias across the load. The Zener keeps the load voltage constant.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: A force F = (5i + 3j) N moves a particle through d = (3i + 4j) m. Calculate the work done.
How is the speed of sound in air affected by temperature, pressure, density and humidity? At what temperature does it become twice its value at 27 °C?
questions.answer:
Temperature: v ∝ √T, so it rises with temperature. Pressure: no effect at constant temperature (P/ρ stays constant). Density: v ∝ 1/√ρ. Humidity: moist air is less dense, so v increases.
For v to double, T must be 4 times: 4 × 300 = 1200 K = 927 °C.

questions.q: An isolated hydrogen atom emits a photon of 9 eV. Find (i) the photon's momentum, (ii) its effective mass and (iii) the recoil velocity of the atom. (m_H = 1.6 × 10⁻²⁷ kg)
questions.answer:
E = 9 × 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ = 1.44 × 10⁻¹⁸ J.
(i) p = E/c = 1.44 × 10⁻¹⁸/3 × 10⁸ = 4.8 × 10⁻²⁷ kg m/s.
(ii) m = E/c² = 1.6 × 10⁻³⁵ kg.
(iii) Momentum is conserved: v = p/m_H = 4.8 × 10⁻²⁷/1.6 × 10⁻²⁷ = 3 m/s (opposite to the photon).

questions.q: Define forward bias and reverse bias. Plot the variation of current with applied voltage for a p-n junction.
questions.answer:
Forward bias: p-side to the positive and n-side to the negative terminal; the barrier is lowered and current flows easily.
Reverse bias: p-side to negative and n-side to positive; the barrier is raised and only a tiny current flows.
Graph: in forward bias the current is almost zero up to the knee voltage (Si about 0.7 V), then rises steeply. In reverse bias a small, nearly constant reverse current flows (µA) until breakdown, when it rises suddenly.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Define terminal velocity and derive its expression for a sphere falling through a viscous fluid. Explain why raindrops do not hurt and why a parachute works.
questions.answer:
Terminal velocity is the constant velocity a body reaches when the net force on it becomes zero.
Forces on a sphere: weight (4/3)πr³ρg down; upthrust (4/3)πr³σg up; Stokes drag 6πηrv up.
At terminal velocity: (4/3)πr³(ρ − σ)g = 6πηrv ⇒ v = 2r²(ρ − σ)g/9η.
Raindrops are small (v ∝ r²) and reach a low terminal speed, so they land gently.
A parachute has a large area, so the drag is large and the terminal speed small, giving a safe landing.

questions.q: Explain how a transistor works as an oscillator. A parallel LC circuit has L = 1 mH and C = 0.1 µF. Calculate the frequency.
questions.answer:
An oscillator is an amplifier with positive feedback. The LC tank in the collector circuit oscillates; part of its energy is fed back in phase to the base through a feedback coil (mutual induction), making up for losses so the oscillations are sustained. No input signal is needed.
Frequency f = 1/2π√(LC) = 1/(2π√(1 × 10⁻³ × 0.1 × 10⁻⁶)) = 1/(2π × 10⁻⁵) ≈ 15.9 kHz.
